entries.title: CI runs the harness on every change; publishing is a dispatched workflow
entries.summary: The eight workflows are five: a staged PR gate whose every job is a required check on main by name, a merge-to-main witness that opens a regression issue per failing Floor, a nightly drift run, CodeQL, and a dispatch-only release workflow with trusted publishing, Test PyPI first, clean-venv smoke on both OSes and a post-publish handshake. Tied search_symbols scores now rank by symbol id on every platform; the token benchmark reference is captured on CI; two new Floors (pyright ratchet, pip-audit zero); SECURITY.md gains a reporting policy. The first release cut through the pipeline.

entries.title: A display preference edited the data it was displaying
entries.summary: Reported by @rknighton, twice: #570 for the crash and #572 for the cause, with a standard-library reproduction that builds its own repo and needs no fixtures. `cache_put` stored the caller's dict and `cache_get` returned that same dict, so the dispatcher's metadata step — a DISPLAY preference — reached into the session

entries.title: A fix for a false positive can install a false negative
entries.summary: `confidence: 1.0` is documented as **provably unreachable**. That is a claim about the tree, and it was computed from the index with nothing in between.

entries.title: A rate written for a future date is wrong for every day before it
entries.summary: `tools` is serialised ahead of system and messages, so every byte of the published tool list sits in the cached prefix -- **4,184 B across six tools**, measured. Changing any of it invalidates that prefix and every turn behind it, for every session on every install. `benchmarks/tier_switch/` priced that at 174
